questions.scenario: During a 10-minute PostgreSQL outage, Kubernetes restarted every instance of the payments API repeatedly, and recovery took longer than the outage. The `db` health indicator was in the liveness group.
questions.question: What should the probe configuration be?
options: Make liveness call the database twice
Keep external dependencies like the database out of liveness; include them in readiness so instances stop receiving traffic but aren't restarted
Put the database in both groups
questions.explanation: Restarting can't fix a database outage. Readiness takes instances out of rotation; liveness should reflect only the process's own health.

questions.scenario: A security scan finds `https://api.bank.example/actuator/heapdump` publicly downloadable.
questions.question: Why is this critical, and what's the fix?
options: It's harmless; heap dumps only contain class names
A heap dump contains everything in memory (tokens, passwords, customer data); expose only needed endpoints, move management to an internal port, secure it, and disable heapdump in production
questions.explanation: Exposed actuator endpoints are a known attack path. Minimise exposure (health, info, prometheus), restrict network access and require authentication for the rest.

questions.scenario: A developer adds a metric `bank.transfers` tagged with `account` (the account number) and `reference`. Prometheus memory usage explodes within a day.
questions.question: What went wrong?
options: High-cardinality tags: every unique account/reference creates a new time series; tag only with small fixed sets such as outcome and channel
The metric name contains a dot
questions.explanation: Each unique tag combination is a separate series. Per-account or per-reference data belongs in logs, traces or the database, not metric tags.

questions.scenario: You need to measure how long calls to the card switch take, including p95 and p99 across all instances.
questions.question: Which Micrometer meter fits?
options: Timer with a percentile histogram published
questions.explanation: A Timer records counts and durations; publishing a histogram lets Prometheus aggregate percentiles across instances correctly.

questions.scenario: During an incident you need DEBUG logs for `ng.itlearning.bank.transfer` for 10 minutes without redeploying.
questions.question: Which Actuator endpoint helps?
questions.explanation: The loggers endpoint reads and changes log levels at runtime. Because it changes behaviour, it must be secured.

questions.scenario: The operations team wants to see how many payment jobs are waiting in an in-memory queue at any moment.
questions.question: Which meter type represents that?
questions.explanation: A gauge reports a current value that can go up and down, such as queue size. Counters only increase.

questions.scenario: Support often asks 'which version and commit is running in UAT?' and nobody knows without checking the CI logs.
questions.question: What's the simplest fix?
options: Generate build-info (and git properties) with the Maven plugins and expose the info endpoint internally
Add the version to every log line manually
Name the jar after the commit
Ask the release manager each time
questions.explanation: Spring Boot reads META-INF/build-info.properties and git.properties and shows them on /actuator/info, giving an instant answer.
